41: ✦The hard part of being 6 weeks pregnant is, of course, that you haven't told anyone yet.✦Your baby's heart now beats with a regular rhythm and blood has started circulating.✦Until birth, your baby's heart will beat about 150 times a minute – twice an adult's rate – some 54 million times in total. The intestines are developing and the tissue that will form the lungs has appeared. The brain, muscles and bones are forming along with the pituitary gland.
42: ✦This week, blood from the mother reaches the baby via the placenta through the umbilical cord.✦The placenta produces hormones that support the baby's development and sends nutrients and oxygen.✦The placenta also helps remove waste from the baby's body.✦Thanks to the filter between mother and baby, they can have different blood types.
43: ✦At 7 weeks your baby is about 10–13 mm long – roughly the size of a bean or a small grape.✦It weighs about 2 grams.
44: ✦This week there's a noticeable jump in your baby's growth rate.✦Your baby grows 2–3 times bigger than last week.
45: ✦This week the baby's face keeps developing more clearly.✦A tiny mouth and tongue start to form.✦Leg buds begin to appear.✦The arm buds from last week grow larger and take on a paddle shape.✦The hands and shoulders begin to form.
46: ✦This week the eyes, nostrils, gallbladder, intestines and pancreas continue to develop more clearly.✦The structures of the ears begin to form.✦The eyelids are almost complete.
47: ✦At seven weeks the joints of the knees, elbows and wrists have formed.✦Other organs continue to develop at the cellular level.✦The baby's sex has been determined at the cellular level.
48: ✦This week the thyroid gland keeps developing.✦The central neural tube separates into the brain and spinal cord.✦The baby's brain grows bigger.✦Nerve cells begin to form that will carry messages from the brain to the body.✦The delicate, interconnected forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain have begun to form.
49: ✦At 7 weeks the right and left heart valves start to develop.✦The heart beats much faster than last week.✦It beats about 180 times a minute – twice an adult's rate.✦Blood circulation has begun.✦The digestive system starts to form as small buds.
50: ✦This week the hands and feet are forming tiny webbed fingers and toes.✦Your baby's tail begins to disappear.
51: ✦In about a month, when there's more room in your baby's belly, the intestines will move from the cord back into the abdomen.
52: ✦As the intestines form and there isn't enough room in the abdomen, a loop moves into the umbilical cord.✦Even at this early stage the intestines carry waste out of the body.
53: ✦Your baby is growing like a storm.✦This week the length has passed 1 cm – at 8 weeks your baby is about 1.4 to 2 cm long.
54: ✦Whoever you choose – obstetrician, family doctor, nurse practitioner or midwife – it's very important to trust their approach and care.✦Visits are usually scheduled once a month, becoming more frequent in the last two months until your baby arrives.✦These regular check-ups are perfect chances to ask questions and share your worries, so come prepared!
55: ✦The tips of your baby's milk teeth are forming.✦Bone cells have started to shape and tiny joints are developing.✦The webbing between the fingers and toes is getting thinner.
56: ✦Your baby is moving inside your belly, but you can't feel it yet.
57: ✦Your baby is now about 2 cm long.✦The eyelids are forming and the ears are developing.✦The tooth roots in the gums continue to take shape.
58: ✦Your baby's hands have now separated into 10 tiny fingers.✦Even though you can't feel it yet, your baby is becoming more active.✦They can move their arms and legs, turn their head and open and close their mouth.
59: ✦Taste buds are starting to form in the mouth and on the tongue.✦While the eyes develop in detail, the nose has become recognizable.✦Your baby's major organs – brain, heart, lungs and kidneys – continue to develop.
60: ✦It's still too early to see the sex on an ultrasound, but small movements can be seen.✦Muscles and bones keep developing.✦At this stage, it's important to support the developing body with vitamin D (ask your doctor).
61: ✦Your baby's eyes are still on the sides of the head; in the coming weeks they'll move toward the middle.✦One exciting milestone is near: this week the eyelids are getting ready to open and close!
62: ✦Your baby can open and close their mouth and turn their head.✦They can move their arms and legs.✦The mother-to-be won't feel these movements yet.
63: ✦Almost all of the baby's organs have started working.✦The digestive system has begun to form.✦The liver is starting to work and the pancreas has started producing insulin.✦The intestines have started moving into their place in the abdomen.✦The four chambers of the heart, beating 160–180 times a minute – twice your rate – formed last week.✦The valves that keep blood flowing through the heart have formed.
64: ✦This week your baby has reached about 3 cm.✦At this stage the brain is developing much faster than other parts.✦The head looks large compared with the rest of the body.
65: ✦Your baby can bend their arms, which helps the muscles develop.✦They can wiggle their newly separated little toes.
66: ✦If you could see inside, you'd see the spine beneath the transparent skin.✦During this period your baby becomes more active during the day.✦Their activity can be described as sleeping and waking states.
67: ✦Along with the developing jawbone, tiny tooth buds are forming.✦Bone and cartilage are developing in the body, and tiny ear canals in the head.
68: ✦This means you've passed a critical period in your baby's development.✦You can take a breath of relief now.✦Most congenital abnormalities appear before 10 weeks of pregnancy.
69: ✦This week, 250,000 neurons are produced every minute.✦That means the brain is developing faster than ever.✦The kidneys produce more urine, and if your baby is a boy, the testes produce testosterone, the male hormone.
70: ✦During this period your baby becomes more active during the day.✦Their activity can be described as sleeping and waking states.
71: ✦Last week your baby entered the fetal stage.✦From now until birth the baby will be called a fetus.✦As the fetus grows this week, the heart rate slows down.✦The heart starts beating more slowly, below 160 beats a minute.
72: ✦The chest and belly slowly start to flatten.✦Organs, including the intestines, keep developing.✦The baby practices breathing by inhaling small amounts of amniotic fluid.✦The skin has become thicker.✦Signs of hair begin under the surface of the skin.
73: ✦As the sense of touch keeps developing, the baby can now respond reflexively to outside stimuli.✦For example, if the mother presses her belly with her hand, the baby may move away by reflex.✦The baby doesn't feel any pain yet.
74: ✦This week the sense of taste also starts to develop.✦All of this shows that the first learning is beginning in the brain.✦Pay even more attention to what you eat and drink.✦Avoid drinks containing substances like caffeine and alcohol, which can stay in your baby's blood for up to 100 hours.
75: ✦The yolk sac, which produces blood cells, keeps shrinking and will disappear over the next few weeks.✦Your baby's vocal cords have also started to form.
76: ✦The lenses of the eyes and the eyelids have formed.✦The eyelids are still closed.✦The facial bones are clearly visible.✦The bones continue to harden.✦The chin becomes more defined.✦The first tooth buds in the jawbone keep developing.
77: ✦At 11 weeks the baby's genitals start to change shape: a clitoris forms in girls and a penis in boys.✦Many mothers-to-be wonder whether the sex can be seen at 11 weeks.✦But it's still too early to guess the baby's sex.
78: ✦Nails have appeared.✦The tiny nail beds have started making nails – get the baby nail clippers ready.✦Most babies are born with long nails that need trimming soon after birth.
79: ✦The truly critical period of your baby's development is coming to an end.✦By the end of this week every body part will be in place; even the genitals will have developed (though it's still too early to tell the sex).
80: ✦Lights out.✦This week the eyelids have formed and will close.✦They'll stay fused until the end of the second trimester.
81: ✦Feed me! Put away the takeaway menus: your appetite is back!✦Around this week many women say they can feel 'the baby is hungry'.✦Make sure you eat enough and keep a healthy diet, but don't think you need to 'eat for two'.
82: ✦What's normal and what isn't? As your blood volume increases to nourish your baby, your gums may feel sensitive and bleed when you brush or floss.✦Although it's uncomfortable, it's completely normal.
83: ✦This week your baby is about 5–6 cm long, the size of a plum.✦It weighs about 13–14 grams.
84: ✦Here's some exciting news while your little one grows: your baby can do acrobatics in the womb.✦This week your baby can climb, turn upside down, stretch backwards and even do somersaults inside your womb.✦They can kick with those tiny legs.✦And practically box with their arms.✦They're probably having a great time in there.
85: ✦This week your baby is about 7–8 cm long, about the size of a lemon or tangerine.✦It weighs about 22–25 grams.
